reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited text supports it: § 12.3 (p0049) affirmatively preserves Customer's right to hire any person responding to general recruitment and records that Customer has made no no-hire commitment, matching the rule's preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer).

No redline and no counterparty comment were proposed, which is the correct output for a compliant finding; the rendered redline is byte-identical to the original paragraph, so there is no directional or drafting error to correct.

The failed deterministic checks (12-month duration, general-solicitation carve-out) test fallback parameters that only apply if a non-solicit binds Customer; since no such covenant exists, these heuristics are non-probative here and the § 12.3 'hiring any person who responds to general recruitment' language in fact functions as the equivalent freedom-to-hire language.

Rationale is accurate and appropriately scoped — it identifies the searched terms, explains that other 'personnel' references (§§ 3.1, 14.2, 30.1) concern Vendor's responsibility for its own staff rather than any hiring restriction, and does not overstate the evidence.
